transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-26 15:00 PT | Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Sofia Romero (CSM) — Daniel Reyes (Greenfield Head of ML), Priya Singh (Infra Lead), Amy Walters (Product), Jamal Carter (Security), Lucas V. (SRE)

Summary: quick kickoff, medium transcription quality, some words garbled (e.g., KV cache became KV case).

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, I'll be owning the onboarding run at Redwood, pairing with Ethan our SE and Sofia on success. Quick roll call?
[00:09] Daniel Reyes: Hey Maya, Daniel here. Excited to get started.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Priya — infra.
[00:14] Amy Walters: Amy from product.
[00:16] Jamal Carter: Jamal, security.
[00:18] Lucas V.: Lucas, SRE.
[00:20] Maya Patel: Great. Agenda — we want to align on pilot scope, network/infra needs, security checklist, and next steps. Ethan over to you for the technical overview.
[00:33] Ethan Liu: Thanks. Briefly: Redwood can ship several deployment options — hosted API for fastest go-live, Dedicated reserved GPU pools if you want predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads. For the pilot we usually recommend starting with hosted to iterate on prompts and evals, then a short smoke test to compare against Dedicated or VPC depending on latency and data requirements.
[01:05] Daniel Reyes: We have PHI-ish data, so we're not comfortable sending raw logs to a multitenant environment. Can you explain encryption and KMS options?
[01:16] Ethan Liu: Sure — for hosted we offer customer-managed KMS keys in supported clouds, and for Private we can run the control plane in your VPC and keys are entirely customer-controlled. There are also options for token redaction and restricted retention windows. Note: need to check SOC 2 scope for hosted with CMK.
[01:37] Jamal Carter: Right — SOC2 plus audit trail retention. We'll want to know which artifacts you can provide and also if you support HSM-backed keys.
[01:47] Maya Patel: We have a security pack we share — I'll attach that after the call. It lists SOC2 reports, pen test summaries, our KMS integrations, and available audit logs.
[01:57] Amy Walters: On the product side we care about latency more than cost initially — devs want sub-200ms p50 for short prompts. Can you get close with the hosted option?
[02:10] Ethan Liu: For short prompts on tuned open models we commonly see ~120–180ms p50 on hosted in US regions, depends on model, quantization, and batching. Dedicated can tighten variance and reduce p99. There's a tradeoff: Dedicated adds commit cost but helps predictability.
[02:31] Priya Singh: If we go VPC, what is the egress pattern? Do you require a NAT/peering? We run strict egress controls.
[02:40] Ethan Liu: For VPC Private, we support VPC peering and private link in some clouds; we can design a no-internet egress path for inference traffic. We'll need CIDR ranges and allowed ports; I'll send a network worksheet.
[03:00] Lucas V.: Also are we able to run in our on-prem air-gapped environment? We heard Redwood has an on-prem package?
[03:07] Maya Patel: Yes, on-prem is possible for larger deals. It is a packaged deployment with an install window. That would be a longer track with additional compliance gates.
[03:20] Ethan Liu: Pilot suggestion — start hosted for prompt iteration with CMK, run a 2-week performance bench with our test suite, and if numbers require, spin up Dedicated or Private for production. For the bench we request a representative prompt set, concurrency profile, and sample token lengths.
[03:40] Daniel Reyes: Makes sense. For pilot success criteria: we propose p50 < 200ms, p95 < 400ms, throughput 50 req/s sustained for 10 minutes, and quality thresholds measured vs our internal label set.
[04:00] Amy Walters: We'll also track hallucination rate on the dev set and require no regression >5% over baseline.
[04:08] Ethan Liu: OK noted.

[04:20] — Topic: Network intake and runbook items —
[04:25] Maya Patel: Action items for network: Priya, we need CIDR ranges, bastion/egress constraints, and whether you want peering or private link. We'll provide a sample Terraform snippet for peering.
[04:40] Priya Singh: We'll share ranges, and we prefer peering if possible. A Terraform snippet would help.
[04:46] Maya Patel: Great.

[05:00] — Topic: Security/compliance —
[05:05] Jamal Carter: Quick Q: do you persist transcripts by default? We need to know retention and options for masking.
[05:14] Sofia Romero (CSM): By default, hosted retains transcripts for 30 days for debugging, but we can request shorter retention or disable retention for the pilot; masking redaction is supported for PII.
[05:27] Jamal Carter: Ok, please include that in the security pack.

[05:35] Ethan Liu: Another nit — if you plan to use continuous batching, that impacts latency distribution; we can tune batching thresholds per-route. For low-latency calls we'd probably set small batch windows and enable prefix caching for repeated contexts.
[05:52] Daniel Reyes: What's prefix caching?
[05:55] Ethan Liu: It's KV cache of previous prompt prefixes — if many requests share similar context, we can cache encoder/kv to reduce compute per token. Sometimes transcript mislabels it KV case in our own notes — sorry, transcription humor.

[06:10] Amy Walters: Pilot timeline — we want to be in a dev pilot in two weeks and a production pilot in six. Is that realistic?
[06:17] Maya Patel: Two-week dev pilot is doable if we get runbook inputs and sample prompts today-ish. Production pilot in six weeks depends on VPC/Legal review, but timeline seems reasonable.

[06:32] — Topic: Billing/pricing and Dedicated commitments —
[06:35] Maya Patel: Quick billing note: hosted usage billed per token for generation and per unit for embeddings; Dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity, we can share cost estimates. We'll send a pricing estimator.
[06:48] Priya Singh: For procurement we need a ballpark for committed GPU monthly cost to compare with self-hosting.
[06:55] Maya Patel: We'll include an apples-to-apples spreadsheet in the runbook — includes expected QPS, token counts, and modeled costs.

[07:06] — 20 minutes later mid-call points (transcript shows pauses and cross-talk) —
[27:10] Ethan Liu: Back to network — for Private deployments we require an initial connectivity window for control plane handshake; that usually takes an hour of network engineers time.
[27:24] Lucas V.: Who manages the HSM integration? Our security team prefers we keep keys on our HSM.
[27:30] Ethan Liu: We support customer-managed KMS, HSM-level keys depending on cloud provider; for full on-prem HSM integration we'd run through our security engineering checklist.

[28:00] Daniel Reyes: Technical deep dive request — can Ethan run a short bench of our top-20 prompts? We'll need log outputs and token breakdowns.
[28:12] Ethan Liu: Yes — we can run a bench on hosted with your prompt set; please anonymize PII in the samples unless you want to set up a Private pilot. We'll send a bench template and expected deliverables.

[30:00] — planning cadence —
[30:05] Sofia Romero: Proposed cadence: weekly check-ins during pilot on Fridays, and a biweekly exec sync.
[30:13] Amy Walters: Fridays work for dev team.

[31:00] — objections and clarifications —
[31:07] Jamal Carter: Concern: audit scope for SOC2 — do you provide signed SOC2 Type II or just attestation?
[31:15] Maya Patel: We can provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA. I'll include the redacted copy in the security pack and follow legal steps.
[31:25] Jamal Carter: Good. Also please list subprocessor vendors.
[31:29] Maya Patel: We'll include that.

[33:00] — risk and fallback policies —
[33:06] Ethan Liu: We recommend a fallback policy: if hosted latency or quality regresses, route to dedicated model variant or older model snapshot. We can configure automatic fallback rules in Redwood Console.
[33:21] Daniel Reyes: Nice. That gives confidence.

[36:00] — next steps recap —
[36:06] Maya Patel: Recap: Redwood to share onboarding runbook, network worksheet, security pack, pricing estimator, bench template. Customer to share CIDR ranges, SSO metadata, representative anonymized prompts, and confirm SOC2 artifact access.
[36:26] Priya Singh: We'll aim to get CIDR and SSO by 2026-07-29.
[36:30] Daniel Reyes: Prompt set by 2026-07-28.
[36:33] Jamal Carter: I'll review SOC2 scope and request docs by 2026-07-31.

[37:00] — closing —
[37:05] Maya Patel: Ok we'll follow up with a calendar invite for weekly Friday check-in starting 2026-07-31 and attach the runbook. Any final Qs?
[37:15] Amy Walters: No, thanks.
[37:17] Lucas V.: No.
[37:18] Ethan Liu: I'll draft the bench plan and ping Priya for infra notes.
[37:23] Sofia Romero: I'll set the calendar and owner tags in our CS tracker.
[37:30] Maya Patel: Thanks all.

[37:35] — End of meeting — occasional transcription glitches: "KV case" for KV cache, "CMK" sometimes transcribed as "C-M-K" —

Action items (as recorded above) and next steps listed.

Keywords: onboarding, VPC, KMS, SOC2, dedicated, hosted API, pilot, latency, bench, runbook.
